content.rendered: A placard includes a visual image written with texts: “Education is Power”, “Resistance Never Futile” and “Read Banned Books”. Slices of watermelon symbolise the colours of the Palestinian flag (red, black, white, and green), representing Palestinian resistance against the Israeli occupation, particularly significant during the 1993 ban on the Palestinian flag. The black and white checkered keffiyeh print is also a symbol of the resilience of Palestinians. Three individuals depicted wearing keffiyehs are shown holding books in the visual imagery in sync with the message of reading banned books.

A placard with text: “We were told these chains were jewelry – Now we’re melting them into weapons”. A printed image that shows an individual breaking the chain is on the left and additional strokes are used to illustrate longer hair. There is a text directly written on the image: “If you want submission, try capitalism not women!” Other words like “chains”, “jewelry” and “weapons” are decorated with colours and symbols.

title.rendered: We were told these chains were jewelry, now we’re melting them into weapons

content.rendered: A placard with text: “Trying to Silence the LGBTQ+ Community? Good Luck Babe!”. The lower side of placard was filled with lipsick print. The text: “Free Palestine” is written at the back.

title.rendered: Trying to Silence the LGBTQ+ Community? Good Luck Babe!
